claims.text: A tailored ab initio framework can improve predictions of low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The expected prediction improvement over conventional models is approximately 20–30%.
The proposed framework explicitly models chemical disorder.
The proposed framework explicitly models multiple phonon-scattering events.
Phonon scattering dominates heat transport under the specified moderate-to-high temperature-gradient conditions.
High-entropy alloys possess inherent chemical disorder.
Chemical disorder and lattice distortions influence phonon-scattering processes in high-entropy alloys.
Conventional models rely on simplified empirical approximations that inadequately represent compositional disorder in phonon transport.
Explicitly simulating chemical disorder resolves a shortcoming of conventional phonon-transport models.
Accounting for multiple phonon-scattering channels improves prediction accuracy for phonon thermal conductivity.
The framework will accurately identify alloys whose phonon thermal conductivity is below the threshold required for efficient thermal insulation.
The approach is applicable to high-entropy alloys within a targeted compositional range.
The approach may become less accurate for alloys with extreme phase separation.
The approach may become less accurate for alloys with non-equilibrium microstructures.
The exact improvement and compositional applicability limits require calibration against a broad experimental dataset.
The hypothesis is falsified if more than 50% of tested alloys deviate by over 30% from the framework's predicted conductivity.
The hypothesis is falsified if the proposed framework fails to show a statistically significant improvement over conventional models.
